oneLineCopy: Everything you ever saved — findable at last.

hero.headlineSerifLead: Bookmarks, shared links and open tabs get read, tagged and connected to whatever you're working on.

founderScenario.story: Daniel is looking for the article on cap tables. He knows he saved it. In Chrome? In the notes app? In that WhatsApp chat with himself? After eleven minutes he googles it again — and finds a worse one.

benefits: A link you save gets read, not just filed
You search for the content, not the title you've forgotten
Saved things resurface where they help: the right project, the right moment
Dead links are caught before you need them
Your reading list sorts itself by what you're working on
howSteps: You save a link — from the browser, from a chat, or by telling your Aven
Your Aven reads the page, summarises it and tags it
The link is connected to topics, people and projects it already knows
Next time that topic comes up, it puts the link back in front of you

whatMechanics.input: Bookmarks, shared links, open tabs and whatever you throw at your Aven
whatMechanics.magic: Page extraction → summary → tagging → linking into the context graph → dead-link detection
whatMechanics.output: A searchable, connected library instead of a bookmarks bar

playsWith.relation: Links hang off the same topics and people as everything else
Shared links arrive through the same entrance
Whatever sits behind the link as a document gets read too
Research is already waiting when you write

standaloneAlternatives.label: Notion Web Clipper + tidying by hand

valueStack.timeDelayToValue: The first saved link is searchable immediately
valueStack.effortToInstall: Import your bookmarks — your Aven does the rest
valueStack.proof: Still in the workshop: bookmark champion runs in our own days before it runs in yours.

bonuses: Contextual reading list: whatever fits your current project comes first
Dead-link warning: vanished pages are archived before they're gone
Resurfacing: what you saved six months ago comes back when it counts
letterFromPublisher: A bookmark is a promise to yourself you almost never keep. Daniel has over 4,000 of them. I'm reading all of them right now — not so he can go through them, but so they can find him when he needs them.
